newsitem.title: EGYPT: Banks pull Egypt market back to record levels.
newsitem.headline: Banks pull Egypt market back to record levels.

text.p: Banks shares pulled the Egyptian stock exchange back to a record close on Monday after a break of two trading days for profit taking.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said the all-share index rose 5.34 points or 1.26 percent to an all-time high of 427.77.

Turnover was a hefty 324.48 million pounds ($95 million) but two thirds of this came from the formal transfer of al-Ahram Beverage shares to Bankers Trust in London for a global depositary receipt (GDR) offering.
Banks greatly outshone other sectors and the traditionally dominant shares -- millers and cements -- were mixed.
Brokers say banks have been especially popular with investors in recent weeks because they are the companies best equipped to take quick advantage of economic expansion.
Misr International Bank (MIBank) ended the day 30 pounds up at 975 pounds and Commercial International Bank (CIB) 46.53 pounds up at 977.29. Both were all-time highs.
In slightly lower volume, Egyptian American Bank and National Societe Generale Bank followed suit.
"But banks can't continue at this pace for long," said Neveen el-Tahry of brokers EAB Delta, referring to the regular gains of five percent a day in the sector.
In cements, Amriyah again benefited from an HSBC James Capel report which identified it as the most attractive stock in the sector. It added 0.50 to end at 90.50.
But Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA, also recommended by the HSBC report, slipped 1.5 pounds to 77.50.
The milling shares, which helped fuel the meteoric rise in share prices this year, faltered again but Tahry said she thought the prices were beginning to stabilise.
Most traded was North Cairo Flour Mills, which reversed some of its recent losses to close 0.74 up at 208.9. The share price had peaked at 234.00 on February 5.
The big real estate companies, Medinet Nasr and Heliopolis Housing and Development, both lost ground.
Tahry said the average P/E ratio for the Egyptian market had just gone beyond 15.5 for the most active shares but it remained relatively attractive by international standards.
"There's nothing to worry about. It went on hold for a couple of days and now it's picking up again," she added.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 753.00 from 732.91 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms increased to 271.23 from 270.73 points.
Out of the 98 shares traded, 45 gained, 30 lost and 23 ended the day unchanged.
